overline.purpose: "Or try one" over the examples, ink, 13 px. Semibold, uppercase, 0.08em.

face-question.purpose: "What goes in the box?" heading the box's face: bold, about 30 px at 1280 by 800, sized with the box, never under 15 px.

face-request.purpose: The request typed on the box's face, in ink: about 26 px at 1280 by 800, shrinking with its length, never under 16 px; muted once sent.

headline.purpose: The product name, top left of the field. Expanded, extra bold, lowercase; 1.375rem on a phone, 1.625rem from 1024 px.

title.purpose: The current question in its card.

body.purpose: The thread, reasons, the text box.

body-small.purpose: Source lines, 'more questions', small buttons, the tracing notice.

label-key.purpose: The factor's name on a label, uppercase, muted, over its value.

label-value.purpose: The answer on a label, bold, lowercase.

hand.purpose: What the app writes on the box only: the first label, what was understood or "?", in capitals.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Arrivals: the label drop, flaps turning out, the scan window opening, the leader line drawing.

motion.name: button-colour
motion.purpose: Fill and border colour changes on buttons and chips.

motion.name: label-drop
motion.purpose: A label dropping onto the box behind its front lip.

motion.name: seal-and-open
motion.value: about 500 to 640 ms, staged per flap, tape and window
motion.purpose: The box sealing and opening; the same rules run both ways.

motion.name: leader-line
motion.purpose: Joins a new panel label to its twin on the box; wide screens with motion allowed only.

motion.name: station-breathe
motion.purpose: The current station of the route line: the page's one looping still-working signal.

motion.name: marker-writing
motion.value: hover: arrive 500ms, bob 1300ms alternate; write: 45ms a character, linear; lift 450ms
motion.purpose: The box's first label: a marker hovers at its start while the request is read, then writes the category and budget, or "?", and lifts away.

motion.name: label-slide
motion.value: 650ms ease-out-expo from 300ms, from the face's top edge, turning at the end
motion.purpose: The blank first label sliding in over the faded request and settling just below it.

motion.name: face-clear
motion.value: heading fades 200ms; request and labels rise 500ms ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The questions asked: the face's heading goes and the request moves to its top, the labels with it, to leave room for five.

motion.name: opening-move
motion.value: 600ms ease-out-expo transition of grid-template-columns (1fr 0fr to 5fr 3fr) and the box's max-width; the request fades to muted over 700ms
motion.purpose: Next on a wide screen: the panel's column opens and the box slides left with it, a layout change; Start again and Edit run it back.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every transition and animation jumps to its end state.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Before the first send the field fills the page, the composer on the box's face and the examples beside the box (below it on a phone); then field and panel side by side (5 to 3). Twelve ticks instead of four, the leader line appears.

components.css: .ds-route { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(5, minmax(0, 1fr)); margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; background: #EF6A4C; color: #17100E; font: 500 0.9375rem/1.2 Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-route::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 7px; border-top: 2px solid #17100E; } .ds-st { position: relative; padding: 26px 8px 0 0; } .ds-done, .ds-now { font-weight: 700; } .ds-st i { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 16px; height: 16px; border: 2px solid #17100E; border-radius: 50%; background: #EF6A4C; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-done i { background: #17100E; } .ds-now i { background: #FFFFFF; } .ds-now i::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: -7px; border: 2px solid #17100E; border-radius: 50%; animation: ds-breathe 2000ms ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-breathe { 50% { opacity: 0.25; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-now i::after { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The purchase is set like a Dutch public information system (Total Design, PTT), painted coral. One open box sits on a coral field. The shopper's criteria become white labels stuck on its front. The box is sealed while the agents work and opened when the answer is ready. Beside it, on a calm off-white panel, the thread does the reading and answering. Before the first message the field fills the page and the box's face is the composer; on Next the request stays on it, faded like pencil, and the app's marker writes what it understood on a label over it.

The page has two modes. The coral half is Experience: large, spare, one object. The panel half is Operate: the same type and palette, smaller and quieter, built for reading and tapping. Every working surface is white paper with a 2 px ink border, square at the corners. State is shown with lines: a dash marks a skipped answer and nothing else, solid is the rule, whatever is moving right now is inverted, and a control that cannot be used now fades.

The world refuses the AI-chat column of bubbles under a centred input, eco-green palettes and nature motifs, retail and deal-site looks, scores and badges, and spectacle (gradients, glow, glass, shadows).
keyCharacteristics: A coral field with one drawn object, beside an off-white working panel.
White paper, 2 px ink borders, square corners, no shadows.
Archivo throughout: expanded and extra bold in lowercase for the wordmark, normal width for work; a marker hand only for what the app writes on the box.
State as line form: solid, inverted, and a dash only for a skipped answer.
Labels slightly turned, as if stuck on by hand.

rules.name: The One Coral Rule
rules.body: Coral is the field and the tape, nothing else. Buttons, chips, links and borders are ink. No coral type, no coral buttons, no coral behind a figure.

rules.name: The Tints Stay Home Rule
rules.body: The flap tints belong to the box. Off the box, only the lip tint appears, and only as a hover or working fill.

rules.name: The Expanded Is For Signs Rule
rules.body: The expanded cut is only for the wordmark. Labels, questions and the thread use the normal width.

rules.name: The One Hand Rule
rules.body: The marker face is for what the app writes on the box and nothing else: the first label. The shopper's own words are never in it; never the panel, a heading or a figure.

rules.name: The Lowercase Sign Rule
rules.body: The wordmark and label values are set in lowercase (the first label is written in capitals). Uppercase is only the label key and the overline.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by a 2 px ink border or a change of ground, never by a shadow, glow or blur.

rules.name: The Line Form Rule
rules.body: State is a border style or an inversion, never a colour code. Dashed is a skipped answer only, inverted is chosen or at work; unavailable fades.

dos: Do put every working surface on paper with a 2 px ink border and square corners.
Do show state with line form: solid as the rule, inverted for chosen or at work, dashed for a skipped answer only; fade what cannot be used now.
Do keep coral to the field and the tape; use ink for every control.
Do set the wordmark in expanded Archivo, extra bold, lowercase; set everything else at normal width.
Do use the shared 3 px ink focus outline at a 3 px offset.
Do make every motion jump to its end state under reduced motion.
Do keep every price and figure in plain body type.
donts: Don't add shadows, glows, blur, glass or colour gradients.
Don't use leaf greens, earth tones or nature motifs.
Don't shape anything like a price tag or a starburst, or put coral behind a price; labels are plain rectangles with no hole or point.
Don't add a progress bar, score, badge or confetti; the "n of 5" numeral is the progress cue.
Don't set the thread as chat bubbles; a user's turn is plain text behind a 3 px ink rule.
Don't add chrome beyond the wordmark and "New search".
